mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: International passport or national identity card of each beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or civil registry office of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate beneficial owner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified articles of association / corporate charter of each corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent commercial registry of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / extract of criminal record for each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national criminal record office of the applicant's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address in the form of a utility bill or bank statement not older than three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed utility provider or authorized credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille; consular legalization required if the origin country is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, managers and ultimate beneficial owners against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list, and the Luxembourg national sanctions list administered by the CSSF. PEPs are additionally screened using the Financial Intelligence Unit's PEP database and reputable commercial screening tools. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, including documented source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval. Automated transaction monitoring, periodic re-screening at least annually, and immediate reporting to the CRF of any suspicious activity are required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be composed of Latin alphabet characters and must be intelligible in French, German, or Luxembourgish. Non-Latin scripts require an official transliteration into Latin characters accompanied by a certified translation. The legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in the company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of receiving a name rejection notification, the applicant's notary may file a written administrative reconsideration request with the Luxembourg Business Registers, attaching a revised name or a definitive ministerial authorization where applicable. If the rejection is sustained, the applicant must file a judicial appeal before the commercial chamber of the Luxembourg District Court within the procedural time limit established by the Luxembourg Code of Civil Procedure. Alternatively, a written consent and waiver from the holder of any conflicting previously registered name may be submitted as a curative measure before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are not prohibited per se, but a SARL engaged in customs AEO supply-chain audit activity may not rely solely on a commercial virtual mailing address. A tangible registered office in Luxembourg is required where statutory records, corporate minutes and fiscal documentation are maintained, and where legal notices can be effectively served. Virtual office services may supplement, but not replace, the physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low-to-moderate baseline risk of 10–20% per annum for routine post-incorporation administrative verification. Because the business scope includes AEO certification and customs supply-chain audit, the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration may conduct unannounced on-site security verification, raising the first-year physical inspection probability to approximately 35–40%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, specifically Articles 710-1 to 710-22 (SARL); complemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts constitutifs) filed electronically with the RCS through the LBR online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For a SARL, the minimum share capital is EUR 12,000. The capital must be fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg bank or notary; the funds are released only after RCS registration of the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founders hereby subscribe to the issued share capital of the Company as set forth in the draft articles of association, each share being fully paid in accordance with Luxembourg law; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at [address], Luxembourg, as the statutory seat and administrative center; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the articles of association be signed and submitted to the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed as manager (gérant) with sole authority to represent the Company, and [Name] be appointed as authorized signatory; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the managers are authorized to open bank accounts and execute all filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and corporate due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS service, online at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the LBR e-filing portal, submit a name availability request, provide the proposed corporate name and intended activities, and reserve the name. Verify that the name does not conflict with existing Luxembourg registered names or protected trademarks.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
Identity documents of founders
Proof of authorized representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or public policy reasons, file one or more alternative names or submit a written consent from the prior trademark or company name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of association (statuts) in French, German, or Luxembourgish, or in English with a certified translation if required. Arrange a meeting before the notary or execute a power of attorney for representation. The notary verifies conformity with the Law of 10 August 1915 and authenticates the constitutive act.
required_dossiers: Authenticated passport or ID copies of all shareholders
Draft articles of association
Residence permits or visas if shareholders are non-EU nationals
Notarized power of attorney if a shareholder does not appear in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises questions on legal clauses, amend the articles and re-execute the notarial act; if a power of attorney is defective, obtain a corrected and legalized power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or the notary's escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary or blocked account in the name of the future company, deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 12,000, and obtain a blocked capital certificate or bank attestation. The certificate will be submitted to the RCS with the registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized or draft articles of association excerpt
Identity of each subscriber
Bank deposit instructions and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further KYC information, provide the complete corporate ownership structure and ultimate beneficial owner declarations; if the deposit is delayed, use a notary escrow account as an alternative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit through the LBR e-portal or through the notary the notarized articles, blocked capital certificate, registered office address declaration, and appointment of manager. Pay the applicable registration fee and obtain an RCS extract with the registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of association
Bank blocked capital certificate
Declaration of the exact registered office address
Manager's signed acceptance and identity document
Proof of payment of LBR registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or provisional refusal, respond through the notary or corporate counsel within the stated deadline, cure missing declarations, and request expedited processing where the delay threatens commercial operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the official electronic gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), automatically generated by the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR automatically transmits the incorporation data for publication in RESA. This publication makes the incorporation effective against third parties and must appear in the corporate file.
required_dossiers: Approved RCS registration extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or contains errors, contact LBR to request correction or expedited publication; provide the RCS extract as interim evidence of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social security and business authorization formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); municipal establishment licensing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for corporate income tax, VAT, and municipal business tax using the corporate identification form. Enroll the manager and any staff with CCSS for social security. If the company occupies commercial premises, verify whether a municipal establishment authorization or occupancy permit is required.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Corporate identification form (Fichier d'identification)
EU identity card or non-EU residence/work permit of manager
Lease contract or registered office agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, present a provisional identification form and obtain a temporary tax registration acknowledgment; if the municipal permit is refused, rectify fire safety or building compliance deficiencies and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 7020 (management consultancy and supply-chain audit services); the Ministry of Economy (General Directorate for SMEs) has no sector-specific operating license for this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no industrial operating license or manufacturing permit is required for pure consultancy and audit services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based consultancy services with no physical manufacturing, no effluent discharges and no hazardous waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific wastewater, VOC or industrial emission thresholds apply to this activity; the company must nonetheless comply with general municipal waste management and office occupational health standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For leased office premises, the municipal fire safety authority may require a fire safety certificate and structural load inspection before occupancy. Employers with staff must submit a workplace safety declaration and register with the Association d'assurance accident (AAA) for occupational accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; online portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity steps: (1) appoint a Luxembourg authorised representative and registered office; (2) file incorporation / deemed establishment with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via MyGuichet to obtain the RCS registration number and national identification number (matricule); (3) submit VAT registration Form 804 to the AEDT within 15 days of commencing taxable activity; (4) non-resident entities without a Luxembourg permanent establishment must complete AEDT VAT registration before performing taxable supplies; no minimum substance requirement applies at registration stage.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an LU SARL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (17%), municipal business tax (up to ~6.75%) and the 7% unemployment fund surcharge, giving an aggregate effective rate of ~24.94% in Luxembourg City; worldwide taxation on residence; no pass-through treatment for an SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections: VAT grouping (assujetti unique, Art. 60 VAT Law); tax consolidation (intégration fiscale, Art. 164bis LIR); participation exemption election (Art. 166bis LIR); option to subject real property transfers to VAT (Art. 44, para. 3 VAT Law). ATAD/ATAD II anti-hybrid rules under Art. 168quater LIR apply mandatorily; no elective hybrid mismatch mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 35,000 EUR annual turnover for the small enterprise exemption (effective 1 January 2025) for Luxembourg-established taxpayers; non-resident suppliers making taxable B2C supplies in Luxembourg must register without any threshold; the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) may cover distance sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL / EN 16931 since 18 March 2022 for invoices to Luxembourg public authorities; B2B e-invoicing not yet mandatory; no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or API-based tax clearance operates in Luxembourg.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU are zero-rated under Art. 53 VAT Law; B2B services (including AEO certification and supply chain audit services, ISIC 7020) supplied to customers established outside the EU fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the Art. 14 place-of-supply rule, provided the supplier obtains the customer's foreign business/VAT registration ID and contemporaneous contract evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (D.A.U./SAD) with Movement Reference Number (MRN) via the ICG-Luxembourg single window
Bill of Lading / CMR waybill / Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank wire transfer proof of payment
Commercial invoice and export packing list
AEO certificate reference (where used to access simplified export procedures)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg Customs (Administration des douanes et accises) performs post-clearance audits under the Union Customs Code (EU Reg. 952/2013); VAT penalties under Art. 66 VAT Law range from administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 plus VAT shortfall penalties of 10% to 100% depending on intent; retrospective clawback of zero-rating applies with monthly interest at 0.9%; deliberate fraud triggers criminal sanctions of 1 to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to EUR 25,000. Luxembourg imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day reference is a commercial/audit benchmark only.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential banking supervision and licensing are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the euro as its domestic currency and maintains full capital and current account convertibility within the framework of Article 63 TFEU. There are no exchange control laws, no mandatory BCL authorisation for foreign direct investment, and no restrictions on reinvestment, dividends, interest, royalties, or capital repatriation for resident SARLs, provided that corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and, where applicable, withholding tax obligations are satisfied. Profit remittances by a SARL are subject to standard dividend distribution procedures and may trigger a 15% Luxembourg withholding tax subject to treaty relief or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption. Non-resident shareholders can remit sale proceeds and liquidation distributions freely once tax clearance and audited accounts, if required, are in place.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements in Luxembourg. Exporters may retain earnings in EUR or any foreign currency, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio or holding period imposed by the BCL. Settlement may be made through TARGET2, SEPA, or correspondent banking channels. Resident entities are required to report cross-border transactions and international positions to the BCL for European System of Central Banks statistical purposes under Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and related BCL reporting protocols; such reporting is purely informational and does not restrict currency use.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational EUR Account
Corporate Operational and Import/Export Settlement Account
Multi-currency Corporate Account with FX Hedging Line
Capital Escrow and Trade Finance Account
Operational EUR Account and Treasury Management Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium-High for EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions that passport their authorization into Luxembourg under the revised Payments Services Directive (EU) 2015/2366 and the Luxembourg law of 10 November 2009 on payment services. The use of non-EU offshore EMIs is materially limited: such entities may not lawfully maintain a payment account or perform domestic payment initiation for a Luxembourg resident corporate without a local branch, agent, or passport from their home EU regulator. The CSSF requires that payment institutions maintain effective AML/CFT governance, transaction monitoring, and a Luxembourg or EU nexus. A Luxembourg SARL may successfully open with Wise if the entity is selected for onboarding, subject to remote identification, underlying business documentation, UBO declarations, and the account being used only for allowable cross-border and domestic payment flows. Full treasury banking, overdraft facilities, foreign exchange trading, and documentary credit services remain outside the scope of most EMIs, requiring a Tier 1 licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg legislation does not impose an absolute physical presence requirement for directors when opening a corporate account. Remote onboarding is permitted by many banks through video identification and electronic signature, provided the procedure meets CSSF AML/KYC circular expectations and the identification is carried out by an authorised professional. In practice, Tier 1 Luxembourg banks often require at least one director or authorised signatory to attend an in-person compliance interview at the bank's premises or at a Luxembourg legal counsel's office, particularly where the SARL is newly incorporated, holds a capital escrow account, or has complex UBO structures. Remote opening becomes considerably easier if the SARL uses an existing Luxembourg professional trustee, law firm, or notary as a conduit, and if all directors undergo an accredited video-identification process compliant with eIDAS and CSSF guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque multi-layer ownership chain involving trusts, foundations, or non-EU registered holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate chart from the Luxembourg trade and companies register (RCS), organisational chart with percentage ownership for each legal entity, trust deed or foundation instrument, consolidated group structure, recent audited financial statements, tax residence certificates, declaration of beneficial ownership filed with the RCS, and a sworn explanation of commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner, director, or ultimate parent appears in a sanction, embargo, or politically exposed person (PEP) database, or originates from a jurisdiction on FATF, EU, or Luxembourg high-risk and non-cooperative lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full name, date of birth, nationality, address, and PEP/sanctions screening results from a recognised compliance vendor; documented legitimate source of wealth and source of funds; corroborating legal documentation for specific PEP exposure, including public-office status and the exact source of any funds; independent negative news search report; explanation of any historical enforcement actions; written AML legal opinion from a Luxembourg or EU-qualified lawyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank perceives inconsistency between the SARL's declared business purpose (management consulting / supply chain audit) and the anticipated cross-border transaction volumes, AEO certification business, or client geography.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated AEO certificate or application file, signed service agreements with non-resident clients, pro-forma invoices, customs audit methodology documentation, internal compliance charter, corporate insurance policies, beneficial ownership registers, and a detailed business plan projecting monthly transaction volumes, counterparties, and settlement currencies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed account is used for high-risk jurisdictions, crypto-asset flows, cash-intensive receipts, or transactions with sanctioned or embargoed countries despite the entity's supply-chain-audit profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed counterparty KYC files, end-user certificates, customs clearance documentation, shipping and logistics contracts, internal policies on export controls and dual-use goods, EU customs tariff classification memos, withdrawal of any crypto-asset-related activity, updated AML/CFT procedure manual, and board resolution confirming prohibition of transactions with high-risk or sanctioned counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from a non-resident parent or shareholder should be executed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for larger amounts into the SARL's euro-denominated operational or capital escrow account held with a Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance instruction must clearly identify the sender and recipient, include the SARL's beneficiary IBAN/BIC, and use an appropriate economic purpose code consistent with BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, typically classified as a capital participation or equity-related transaction. The bank will require the notarial or private deed of capital increase or contribution, the signed board/shareholder minutes, an updated RCS extract, proof that the applicant funds have not been obtained illegally, and a source-of-funds declaration. No prior BCL exchange-control authorisation is required. The funds are generally credited immediately upon compliance checks, and any anti-money-laundering hold will be released once the documentary package is complete.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for consultancy fees, supplier settlements, and operational expenses are cleared primarily through TARGET2 and SWIFT. Standard SWIFT MT103 messages are appropriate for direct payments in EUR and convertible currencies. For documentary trade flows, commercial letters of credit may be issued via SWIFT MT700, amended via MT707, and settled in accordance with UCP 600; the Luxembourg bank may also handle documentary collections under URC 522. Euro-denominated payments to EU beneficiaries can be made via SEPA Credit Transfer with settlement value on the same business day. All payments must be supported by underlying contracts, invoices, customs declarations, AEO status certificates, and, where relevant, the commercial documentation required by the Luxembourg bank for anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance. Treasury staff should ensure the correct IBAN/BIC, tax reference data, and purpose codes are used to avoid delays or BCL statistical misclassification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX spot contracts executed at prevailing market rates with no exchange-control restrictions
FX forward contracts (outright and cash-settled) for fixed-date synthetic EUR and cross-currency requirements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less-liquid currencies not directly deliverable in the Luxembourg market
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) to hedge both principal and interest exposures on cross-border financing
FX options and zero-premium collars to hedge adverse currency movements while retaining beneficial upside
Currency swaps under ISDA/CSA or local Luxembourg market standard documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (including balance sheet and profit/loss account) filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year; accounting reference date typically 31 December (year-end filing deadline: 30 June next year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of EUR 100 to EUR 500 per day (up to a cap); repeated non-filing triggers court summons and possible administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration of the sole director / manager of the SARL confirming compliance with corporate formalities (annual report and corporate registry update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS via the registered office or authorised representative (e-file via Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after approval of annual financial statements; must be filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; late filing prevents issuance of RCS certificate of good standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Corporate Income Tax, Municipal Business Tax, and Net Wealth Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Luxembourg tax office (bureau d'imposition)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December of the following calendar year for financial year ending 31 December; automatic extension available via e-file until 31 March of second year if requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.2% per month on unpaid taxes; late filing penalties between EUR 100 and EUR 1,000; persistent failure activates enforced collection and seizure of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (obligatory for all VAT registrants, even if no taxable activity for a given period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 1 May for the preceding calendar year (for entities on annual reporting period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty from EUR 100 to EUR 1,000 plus interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid VAT; serious or repeated failure may result in criminal fine and forced closure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE) annual confirmation / update filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following any change; at minimum confirm no change annually by 31 January of next calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250; courts may impose imprisonment for repeat offenders; company may be prevented from distributing dividends until filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statistical report for the balance of payments and international trade in services (BOP survey) if applicable to AEO consultancy operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 business days after each month/quarter-end; annual summary due by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 for non-compliance under BCL reporting obligations; may trigger licence reviews for regulated activities

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if the SARL exceeds two of the following three criteria at balance sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. Entities below all thresholds may be exempt but must still prepare annual accounts
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (as per Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and annual accounts); consolidated entities must apply IFRS if listed

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must identify natural persons owning >25% shares or exercising control; shareholding transfers must be reported to the RBE within 1 month of any change. An annual confirmation (even if no change) is required by 31 January each year, including full legal name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, and nature/scope of beneficial ownership
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (as filed with RCS, maintained by the managing director)
Minutes of Shareholders' General Meetings and Board Decisions
Register of Pledges and Usufruct over shares

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 800-2,500 per annum for a registered office provider in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000-12,000 for a mandatory audit of a small-to-medium SARL, depending on complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% national corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) plus 7% solidarity surcharge, plus municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) of 6.75% in Luxembourg City; aggregate combined statutory effective rate approximately 24.94% for a taxpayers in Luxembourg City.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays in Luxembourg. Principal incentives: participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains (100% exemption where the SARL holds 10% or more or an acquisition price of at least EUR 1.2 million of the distributing company and holds it for 12 months; capital gains require a 10% holding or EUR 6 million threshold held 6 months); research and development tax credit at 20% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 300,000 and 9% on any excess; unlimited carryforward of tax losses with full offset of the taxable base from fiscal year 2023.
